title: Titrate to the first permanent pink: stopcock to a drip, swirl the flask, shut it as the colour holds
instruction: Titrate the acid in the flask with the burette to the first permanent pink: swirl the flask while you add the titrant, and close the stopcock as soon as the pink colour stays.
context: Manual acid-base titration with a glass burette is a standard wet-lab assay in teaching, research and QC labs, done exactly this way: one hand holds the stopcock key at a drip, the other swirls the flask under the tip, and the key is shut at the first pink that does not fade. The difficulty is physical: the key goes from closed to a stream within about 13 degrees, so a drip is a ~10 degree window held by a wrist roll against the key's friction; the flask must be swirled in small circles while the burette tip sits 1 cm inside its neck (7.5 mm clearance); and the key must be shut within a few drops of the end point, which differs every trial (8-12 mL, not told). Colour guides when to slow and stop; the score comes from how far past the end point the flask ends (real trials: a pH meter). Real trials use dilute, nonhazardous solutions (0.05 M NaOH, diluted vinegar) in clamped glassware, with finger cots and a drip tray.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top (x forward, y left, z up); arms in the ready pose. Retort stand: cast-iron base 25 x 16 x 1 cm centred at x 34.5, y 0, clamped to the bench; 12.7 mm rod 70 cm tall at x 44, y 0; burette clamp with rubber jaws 45 cm up. Burette: 25 mL class B borosilicate, PTFE key, 620 mm long (e.g. Pyrex 329504), vertical at x 30, y 0, tip 12.0 cm and stopcock axis 17.5 cm above the table; turned in its clamp so the key's axis points 35 degrees toward -y from x (handle to barrel): the white winged PTFE handle (32 mm span, 5 mm thick) faces the left arm, 2.2 cm from the burette axis; closed = handle horizontal across the burette. Filled to 0.00 mL with 0.05 M NaOH. White ceramic tile 152 x 152 x 6 mm on the stand base under the tip. Flask: 125 mL narrow-mouth borosilicate Erlenmeyer (Pyrex 4980-125, 67 mm base, 114 mm tall, neck 29 mm outside, 21 mm bore) on the tile under the tip, tip 1 cm inside the neck; holds 8.00-12.00 mL of 0.05 M acetic acid (white vinegar diluted 1:16.6; the amount set by the seed and recorded by the technician), water to about 30 mL, 3 drops of 1% phenolphthalein; colourless. Nothing else on the table. Rig protection: drip tray with bench paper under the stand, nitrile finger cots on the pads (README). The screenshot's inset (top right) is a zoom of the boxed area: the white key handle, the burette tip and the flask on the tile.
scoring: Latched over the whole trial, any one gives 0: the flask's glass touches the burette tip (real: video, tip checked for chips); the flask tilts past 45 degrees (video); any titrant falls outside the flask (a drop on the tile, tray or paper, photo); the burette runs empty. Also 0 if titrant still flows at the end (real: a drop falls within 30 s). Otherwise, with T the burette reading and V_e the trial's equivalence volume, once mixed: past the end point (sim: pink, 0.02 mL past V_e) and T - V_e <= 0.30 mL (6 drops): 1.0; <= 1.0 mL over: 0.6; <= 3.0 mL over: 0.3; further over: 0; short but T >= V_e - 1.0 mL: 0.3; T >= V_e/2: 0.1; else 0. Real trial: pH meter (0.01 pH, calibrated with pH 4/7/10 buffers) in the poured-out, swirled liquid; the same bands are pH 8.4-10.6: 1.0; 10.6-11.1: 0.6; 11.1-11.55: 0.3; above 11.55: 0; 5.7-8.4: 0.3; 4.8-5.7: 0.1; below 4.8: 0 (README gives the calculation). Success = 1.0 held 1 s at the end.
reset_notes: Close the key. Empty, rinse and dry the flask's neck. Refill the burette to 0.00 mL and clear the tip of bubbles. Dispense the next seed's aliquot (second burette, or by mass on a 0.01 g balance), add water to about 30 mL and 3 drops of indicator, stand the flask on the tile's marked outline under the tip; check the handle faces the left arm (tape mark on the clamp). About 2 minutes. Standardise each new batch of solutions with three manual titrations before the session.
fidelity: Approximate. Stand, burette and tile are fixed; the flask is a rigid body (stacked-cylinder colliders); the key is a rigid body on a revolute joint with a 0.05 N m stick-slip friction torque (inertia raised for stability). No fluid simulation: a reduced-order model gives flow from the key's bore overlap, 0.05 mL drops or a stream, swirl-driven mixing, a lingering flash near the end point and the bulk colour; its constants are chosen, not measured. The tip has no collider: contact is latched.
